headline: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics resolve cell types, isoforms and tissue layers
label: Single Cell And Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Recent reports extend cell atlases, spatial isoform sequencing and long-read profiling to human, mouse, cattle and killifish tissues.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving cellular and molecular heterogeneity in tissues by coupling single-cell or spatial readouts with higher resolution or additional modalities. Tabula Sapiens 2.0 extends a reference transcriptomic atlas across more than two dozen human organs and tissues. Spatial platforms appear in several items: GeoMx DSP provides layer-resolved profiles of human retina from post-COVID-19 donor tissue, Stereo-seq at 500 nm yields a cattle liver resource with bin-size evaluation, and a spatial tri-omic taxonomy of human hippocampus combines proteomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic data. Spl-ISO-Seq2 adds 500-nm spatial long-read isoform sequencing, revealing cell-type-specific isoform variability in mouse brain. Other items apply single-cell RNA-seq to diabetic corneal epitheliopathy, implicating BHLHE40 and THBS1, and VINE-seq to brain vasculature, while a killifish long-read study improves transcript annotation.
